title: The Way I Came
subtitle: Blood and tears become one, as she weeps in the dark.

items.text: The Way I Came
Altar, Sanctuary
A lump of dark flesh pulsates like a heart, its flowing black fluid spilling into the well, mixed with rain with neither weight nor wetness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That lump of flesh is Arcana?

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: The threads ... They were drawn away somewhere deep below me. This—this isn't right.
She reaches to steady the spindle, only for golden wounds to bloom across her fingertips.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: And the Wheel ... I can't seem to stop it.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin, you must leave.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Spare me the theatrics.
Animus swings her longbow. Black, viscous liquid twists into bonds that pin them both in place.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: The ritual has begun. The Mother will return! Such a moment is not to be disturbed!
Step by step, Animus approaches. Through the chanting, she plucks a white bone from the water.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: These bones are relics of a sacred age—primal, elegant, powerful, just like the era to which they belong.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: They are but a fraction of the creatures from a time erased from history, from the Blank Era.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: The moment is nigh. From the embryo, the Great Mother shall rise once more to restore what was lost!

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: And break the shackles that were forced upon us eons ago!

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: A Blank Era? Restore what was lost? No. Time should move forwards, not backwards!

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: It seems your blindness is not just of the eyes, but of the mind. Still, I shall forgive your blasphemies. You were the one to start the ritual, after all.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: In fact, your contribution should be commemorated with a title. "The Unseeing Saint," perhaps? It is rather fitting, don't you think?

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: No, I ...

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I must stop the Spinning Wheel.
Dores's hand shakes with pain as she reaches out once more, desperate to stop the turning.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Please! Stop!

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Not while I still draw breath!

Animus's longbow strikes the ground with a resounding crash, sending a quake through the entire sanctuary. Responding to her command, threads coil out and around Dores's body, pulling taut around her weakened frame.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Ugh!
The ritual's glow intensifies, while her face grows paler still. As the golden light fades, she collapses into the swirling mist.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: *sigh of relief* Heh ... For a moment, I thought you might've succeeded as you did in 1999.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: But it seems your prime has passed.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: The Mother of Resurrection will soon grace us with THEIR presence. Your fate is inevitable.
With a swing of the longbow, Animus encases Dores in black mucus, dragging both her and the Spinning Wheel down into darkness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores!

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Oh, there's no need for haste, girl. The Mother shall welcome you both into THEIR embrace.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: It is a great honor to become one with THEM. You ought to be grateful.
Animus turns to her weeping believers, still chanting hymns as the rising liquid engulfs them.
A liquid devoid of weight or wetness.
Behind them, an arcane item about to activate is violently struck down.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Well, that was amusing. But that's quite enough folly for one day.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: You think too highly of yourself, just like that bullheaded fool who threw herself to the gate.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: But she realized her error, paid the price in her blood, and thus has been forgiven.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: If it is redemption you seek, then you must first make an offering of yourselves. The Mother, in THEIR great mercy, shall alleviate you of your suffering.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nonsense. Nautika didn't enter the gate to gain forgiveness. She died for her beliefs.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: My, how ignorant of me. Do send her my apologies. After all, you'll be seeing her very soon.
The ropes tighten in a sharp heave.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Surrender unto THEM your flesh and blood, and pave the path to the Mother's return!
Through her obscured vision, the viscous hands from beyond the gate surge through the endless tube, grasping out over the mountain's heart with terrifying speed.
Suffocation strikes instantly.
Woooo—wooooo—
The distant howl of wind escapes the sanctuary's gaping maw.

items.speaker: Animus
items.text: Enter into the Mother's embrace, and THEY shall reward you with THEIR great might!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *coughing*
Vision tinged with red.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *coughing*
It's a warm place, like a mother's embrace.
Open your eyes, that the dream may go on.
Relax, Vertin. The best is yet to come!
Wait till we take a breath of the real air, till we stuffed ourselves with delicious food, and till we get back to our country.
There's so much more for us to be shivering at, but in excitement!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That voice ... It's ...
She moves toward the source of the sound, straining to hear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "The Ring"? Is that you?

items.speaker: Student I
items.text: Let's open it together.

items.speaker: Student II
items.text: Three, two, one—

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: May the freedom be with us!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Isabella, "Penny" ... Are they all here?

items.speaker: Student I
items.text: Let's goooo!

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Vertin! Come outside!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait!

items.speaker: Schneider
items.text: Let's hear everyone's wishes. How about that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Schneider?

items.speaker: Schneider
items.text: My lord, you're actually lying here defenseless. Heh Heh.

items.speaker: Schneider
items.text: We have been with you for a long time. No reward? No way.
A soft, raspy voice drifts away like a feather.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: I find myself uncertain of which way to go. Would you kindly give me some guidance?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Marta? No, but ...

items.speaker: Six
items.text: The guidance I can offer you is limited, Ms. Marta.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: I think fate knows its own fate better than anyone.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: Thank you for your advice.

items.speaker: Marta
items.text: I think I understand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, don't go!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why must I endure this time and time again?
For what was lost need not remain so.
Step forward. Return to us. Our arms are open. Come into the warmth of our embrace.
Her feet carry her toward the sound, then stop.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. This isn't right.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is the way I came.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There are so many things to be done, so many questions to be answered.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: My calling lies elsewhere.
She turns. Faint murmurs beckon from another direction.
Ver ...
And so she strides forward.
Vertin!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where am I?
The dreamlike haze evaporates into an endless darkness.
The walls pulse like living tissue; each step slides over bones slick with gore, submerged in a mix of blood and bile.
The space throbs, each throe spewing another wave of nauseating stench into the abyss.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Am I inside the gate?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are these the offerings? Ugh!
Be careful. One wrong move, and you'll end up like them.
Then, a child's voice, shrunk and rasped with tears, pierces through. The only faint glow in the dark.
That's the only reality in this place.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Who's speaking?
I wish I could tell you, but I don't know either. I can't seem to remember my name, or anything, really.
I've just been waiting here because I wasn't ready to join them.
You seem to still remember a few things. How did you get here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I was thrown to the gate as an offering.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have to get out of here. Do you know a way out?
A way out? I-I really have no idea.
Maybe I can help you find a way. But where do you want to go? Why do you want to go?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I need to exit through the gate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm searching for an answer, and I won't find it here.
An "answer"?
Is that why you were thrown in here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You could say that.
And you're still looking for it? Even after everything that's happened to you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not sure.
What if, what if the "answer" doesn't exist? What if you finish your journey and find out there's nothing out there?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I've asked myself that question more times than I can remember.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sometimes, it feels like I'm doing all this in the pursuit of a mirage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But I've come to be at peace with that possibility.
Really? But what about all the time and energy you put into it?
How do you keep going, knowing that it all could be for nothing?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But it isn't for nothing.
Memories flash before her eyes.
Those sacrifices, those struggles, those who gave meaning to her path.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I carry everything, everyone, with me.
They were real.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So, even if in the end, the path I walk leads me nowhere, I know that ...
"I will pursue the unknown, no matter where it takes me."
The light trembles, uttering these words in a soft yet resolute voice.
Ah, that's it.
That's the answer I was looking for.
The faint light flickers again, brighter this time.
I remember now. I used to have the same belief.
That's why I'm still here, why I wasn't gobbled up by this place.
Because I died content. I died knowing I had chased the answer with all I had.
The light—no, it should now be called a "mass of light." It pulses closer, radiating warmth.
Come, take my hand!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Your hand?
Yes. Here, reach into my heart. There's something there, something I need you to find.
She reaches into its core, and a comforting softness settles in her palm.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It feels like fabric?
No, not that. It's somewhere deeper.
Yes! There!
Uncurling her fingers, she reveals a pendant resting there, its tiny crystal reflecting light that shouldn't exist.
That's it. That's what I needed you to find.
My purpose.
A faint warmth seeps through the pendant, its surface etched with that familiar name.
"Amundsen."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika? Is that you?
Oh, that's it! "Nautika"! That's my name!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Thank you, thank you, Vertin. I found it. I found my name!
Flesh begins regenerating from the glowing mass.
Then, invisible hands grasp her.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: "The path to home, held fast in night's tight grip. Unloosed by breath, a name spoke on the lip."
As she speaks each word, the surrounding scene again begins to warp and dissolve.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The Mother Spirit may not be here, but in my dream, She came to me and showed me the way out.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Come, Vertin. Come. Let's get out of here.
She clutches Nautika's hands. Even in hell, those slender fingers remain strong.
Her body is dissolving, her vision darkening, as if the world itself were rejecting her.
Yet even in annihilation, their hands stay locked together.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Take my eyes, and I will walk blind. Take my feet, and I will crawl on my hands and knees. Take my body ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And I will grow another.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Because nothing will keep me from my purpose. Nothing will keep me from finding the great gift!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Vertin, we did it!
And the world's rebirth stirs within the wind.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are we in the air?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika, look at you!
Black mucus extends out from her body, forming bones, while white fabric weaves itself into wings.
A drum seems to beat from afar. She stretches her wings wide, catching the wind beneath them.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Oh, I look just like the Mother Spirit when She came to me in the dream.
Chin lifted in pride, she shatters the boulders that line the sanctuary. She leaps, and the wind follows.
Then, she rides that wind upward, breaking free from the countless grasping hands.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And—Vertin, look! I have wings! I can fly! I can take us home!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Watch out!
She flaps her wings, dodging the flying debris, and turns toward the source of danger.
Deep within the sanctuary, tremors pulse outward.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Wh-What is that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Arcana.
Throbbing black flesh stretches over countless hands, fusing snugly with the stone walls. The entire sanctuary breathes like a living thing.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If the gate is the mouth, and inside it is the stomach ...
The wind courses through and around, carrying soft whispers with it. Until, all at once, it dives into the flesh.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then, it seems the ruins themselves are alive.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And Arcana is its very heart.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I fear it's only a matter of time before she's fully resurrected.
TO BE CONTINUED…
